question: Under what assumptions can sparse attention transformations be represented exactly as Nadaraya-Watson regression with compact-support kernels, and do the resulting adaptive-bandwidth or max-anchored kernels improve small-model language modeling, in-context learning, and length extrapolation over dense Gaussian/softmax and fixed top-k alternatives?

key_findings.claim: With unit-normalized queries and keys, familiar attention maps form a single kernel-regression family: softmax is Gaussian, normalized ReLU is fixed-bandwidth Epanechnikov, sparsemax is auto-normalized Epanechnikov, and alpha-entmax with alpha = 1 + 1/r is an auto-normalized order-r rectified-polynomial kernel.
key_findings.evidence: The distance identity ||k_i-q||^2 = 2-2k_i^Tq converts radial kernels into score functions. Proposition 1 then derives [1-||u||^2/h^2]^r_+ and identifies r=1,2,3 with Epanechnikov, biweight, and triweight (alpha=2, 1.5, and 4/3); Gaussian/softmax is recovered as r tends to infinity (alpha tends to 1).

key_findings.claim: The exact normalized-ReLU/Epanechnikov construction is not globally well-defined: all negative preactivations produce an empty support and a 0/0 denominator; the experiments silently resolve this by returning uniform weights, which changes the stated sparse rule into a dense fallback on precisely the degenerate cases.
key_findings.evidence: Section 3 explicitly flags the undefined denominator. Appendix B.1 specifies uniform weighting when no key is selected, so the implemented baseline is not the unqualified mathematical map in Equation 6.

anchors.section: 3 Sparse Attention via Compact Kernels, Equation 6

key_findings.claim: ReLUmax is a nonempty-support alternative whose threshold is anchored to the maximum score rather than to a fixed cardinality: an r-ReLUmax head retains scores above m-bh^2 and assigns rectified polynomial weights, guaranteeing that the maximum-scoring key survives when b is positive.
key_findings.evidence: Section 3.2 derives the adaptive bandwidth from the maximum dot product m and contrasts the resulting variable-cardinality support with uniform kNN and top-k Gaussian, which always retain exactly k keys.

key_findings.claim: The empirical object is Memory Mosaics rather than ordinary Transformer self-attention, so the evidence does not establish that compact kernels transfer unchanged to standard query-key attention.
key_findings.evidence: The architecture uses a contextual associative memory with tied query/key representations and a separate persistent memory; its value stream uses a one-step look-ahead because the contextual diagonal is excluded. Experiments replace only the contextual Memory Mosaic kernel, while the Transformer appears as a baseline rather than as a compact-kernel host.

key_findings.claim: On BabiStories, adaptive compact kernels improve validation-loss curves at one and eight layers, but the advantage largely disappears by 12 layers and no exact terminal loss, uncertainty, or statistical test is reported.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 2 shows sparsemax and alpha-entmax curves below Gaussian and top-k variants in the shallow models. At 12 layers, the paper says all methods except normalized ReLU and uniform kNN are roughly tied; 2-ReLUmax at eight layers also required a special lower learning rate because of instability.

key_findings.claim: RegBench supports, at most, a small adaptive-sparsity advantage: at 40k examples biweight 1.5-entmax reaches 95.5% accuracy and 13.8 TVD versus Gaussian Memory Mosaics at 95.4/14.2 and a standard Transformer at 95.5/13.9, while normalized ReLU and uniform kNN are substantially worse.
key_findings.evidence: Table 1 reports biweight 1.5-entmax at 93.8/33.0, 94.3/19.2, 94.7/16.6, and 95.5/13.8 for 1k, 2.5k, 5k, and 40k. Gaussian is 93.9/34.1, 93.7/20.8, 94.6/17.7, and 95.4/14.2; normalized ReLU moves from 84.3/43.6 to 93.3/18.6 and uniform kNN from 84.6/41.1 to 86.4/26.4. Hyperparameters were tuned on Gaussian and transferred to other kernels, with k=16 tuned only on 1k.

key_findings.claim: Length extrapolation is strongly task-dependent rather than uniformly superior: compact kernels dominate MQMTAR at long lengths, the standard Transformer is best on reverse at 1.5x, and the best sorting result at 4x is only 0.34 mean exact match.
key_findings.evidence: At MQMTAR 64x, sparsemax obtains 0.31 versus Gaussian 0.00 and Transformer 0.00. On reverse 1.5x, Transformer obtains 0.52 versus at most 0.29 for triweight 3-ReLUmax. On sorting 4x, biweight 2-ReLUmax reaches 0.34, versus 0.30 for 1- and 3-ReLUmax, 0.29 sparsemax, 0.07 triweight entmax, and 0 for Transformer/Gaussian.

key_findings.claim: Three-seed means conceal material instability in the synthetic tasks, weakening method rankings based on tenths of exact-match accuracy.
key_findings.evidence: Table 2 gives both means and seed maxima. For example, 1-ReLUmax sorting at 4x has mean 0.30 but maximum 0.91; sparsemax has 0.29 mean and 0.79 maximum, while triweight 3-ReLUmax has 0.30 mean and 0.62 maximum. No standard deviations or per-seed results are supplied.

key_findings.claim: Adding ALiBi hurts the Epanechnikov Memory Mosaic on MQMTAR, and the appendix comparison does not isolate kernel sparsity from architecture because its dense comparator is a Transformer with ALiBi.
key_findings.evidence: At 64x, Epanechnikov Memory Mosaics score 0.31 without ALiBi and 0.14 with ALiBi; at 32x the figures are 0.63 and 0.43. Transformer+ALiBi reaches 0.00 at both. The claim that compact kernels, rather than architecture, explain the difference is therefore confounded.

key_findings.claim: The paper demonstrates representational sparsity, not practical efficiency: it reports neither support density, FLOPs, memory, throughput, nor wall-clock speedup and explicitly says gains are modest in its short-context regime.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix B.4 states that 512-token language modeling and few-thousand-token synthetic tests do not make attention the dominant cost. It points to AdaSplash compatibility and possible long-context gains but performs no efficiency benchmark of its own.

key_findings.claim: The appendix-only Simple English Wikipedia check is qualitative and does not support a precise OOD advantage.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 5 plots EMA-smoothed token-position loss at context length 512 without exact values, sample count, seeds, or uncertainty. The text says compact kernels are comparable to Gaussian and calls ReLUmax best overall, but the plot is the only evidence.

key_findings.claim: The conclusion's claim of generally superior performance is broader than the results warrant.
key_findings.evidence: The 12-layer language-model curves are approximately tied; RegBench differences against Gaussian and Transformer are mostly fractions of a point; Transformer wins reverse extrapolation; and the paper provides no large-model, long-context throughput, vanilla-Transformer compact-kernel, or statistical-significance study.

method.core_idea: Treat attention as a Nadaraya-Watson estimate and design sparsity by replacing the Gaussian kernel with bounded-support radial kernels. After unit normalization converts squared distance into an affine dot product, classical compact kernels map algebraically to sparse attention activations.
method.mechanism: For score s_i=k_i^Tq, fixed-bandwidth Epanechnikov produces normalized [s_i/gamma+b]_+. Choosing bandwidth so the denominator is constant yields sparsemax; the order-r family [1-||k_i-q||^2/h^2]^r_+ yields alpha-entmax for alpha=1+1/r. A second family fixes support with k-nearest-neighbor truncation (uniform kNN or truncated-Gaussian top-k softmax). ReLUmax instead anchors the threshold to m=max_i s_i, retains s_i>m-bh^2, raises positive gaps to power r, and normalizes. The experiments insert these kernels in the contextual associative memory of Memory Mosaics, which ties query and key representations, excludes the diagonal, shifts values one token forward, and combines contextual and learned persistent memories.
assumptions: All formal radial-kernel correspondences assume every query and key has unit Euclidean norm; without this, dot-product score thresholds do not equal fixed radial distance thresholds.
The Nadaraya-Watson view assumes attention is a normalized weighted average of values and that its denominator is nonzero; fixed normalized ReLU violates the latter in empty-support cases.
The alpha-entmax correspondence uses alpha=1+1/r with integer r>=1 for the named Epanechnikov/biweight/triweight kernels, although alpha-entmax itself is defined more broadly.
Sparsemax/entmax auto-normalization chooses a data-dependent bandwidth through the normalization threshold; ReLUmax additionally requires b>0 to guarantee the maximum-scoring key is retained.
Top-k equivalences presume a radius that admits exactly k neighbors; ties at the cutoff require a selection convention not analyzed in the paper.
Empirical conclusions assume the Memory Mosaic architecture is an adequate proxy for attention generally, despite its tied contextual query/key map and persistent-memory pathway.
Language-model comparisons assume curve-level validation loss is sufficient despite no exact endpoint table, seed dispersion, or matched-compute efficiency measurements.
The proposed computational benefit assumes an implementation such as AdaSplash can exploit realized support sparsity at longer contexts; realized sparsity is not measured here.

techniques.role: Turns attention weights into normalized kernel weights so activation choices can be analyzed as kernel shape and bandwidth choices.
Uses ||k-q||^2=2-2k^Tq to translate radial compact support into dot-product thresholds.
Chooses the compact-kernel bandwidth through the entmax normalization threshold, producing variable support without an empty denominator.
Anchors support to the largest score, guarantees at least one selected key for positive bias, and permits variable support size.
Reinterprets uniform top-k and top-k softmax as uniform-kNN and truncated-Gaussian regression baselines with fixed support cardinality.
Trains at length 64 and tests up to 64x longer on controlled associative recall, reversal, and sorting to expose task-specific generalization.

evaluations.setting: BabiStories language modeling in Memory Mosaics (p. 7, Section 4.1; p. 15, Appendix B.1): GPT-2 tokenizer; train 2.2M stories/474,704,907 tokens; validation 2.2k stories/4,749,107 tokens; context 512; 1/8/12 layers; width 768; 12 heads; persistent-memory size 2688; 80k iterations; total batch 512; Adam beta=(0.9,0.95), weight decay 0.1, cosine schedule and 2k warmup. Learning rate is 5e-3 at 1/8 layers and 1e-3 at 12 layers, except unstable 8-layer 2-ReLUmax is reduced to 1e-3.
evaluations.metric: Validation cross-entropy loss versus iteration (Figure 2 curves; no exact terminal values or uncertainty).
evaluations.result: Adaptive sparsemax/entmax compact kernels are visibly lower at 1 and 8 layers; by 12 layers most methods are approximately tied except worse normalized ReLU and uniform kNN. Top-k Gaussian shows mild instability.
evaluations.baseline: Gaussian/softmax Memory Mosaics, Gaussian kNN k=32, uniform kNN k=32, normalized ReLU, ReLUmax orders 1-3, sparsemax, 1.5-entmax, and 4/3-entmax.

evaluations.setting: RegBench in-context learning (pp. 7-8, Section 4.2; p. 16, Appendix B.2): random probabilistic finite automata, 10-20 strings per sequence, held-out automata, test set 1,000; train sets 1k to 40k; maximum 200 epochs, batch 32, learning rate 5e-4. Gaussian Memory Mosaic grid-searches weight decay {0.1,0.01}, depth {2,4,8}, width {32,128,256}, and heads {1,2,4,8}; that choice is transferred to other kernels. k in {16,32,64} is tuned on 1k, selecting 16. Lowest-validation-loss epoch reported; one A6000 GPU.
evaluations.metric: Last-token accuracy percent (higher) and total variation distance (lower).
evaluations.result: At 1k/5k/40k, biweight 1.5-entmax is 93.8/33.0, 94.7/16.6, and 95.5/13.8; sparsemax is 94.2/32.5, 94.4/17.1, and 95.4/14.0. Gaussian Memory Mosaic is 93.9/34.1, 94.6/17.7, and 95.4/14.2. Normalized ReLU is 84.3/43.6 to 93.3/18.6; uniform kNN is 84.6/41.1 to 86.4/26.4.
evaluations.baseline: Standard Transformer (54.5/62.6 at 1k; 95.5/13.9 at 40k), Gaussian Memory Mosaics, kNN variants, RetNet, H3, GLA, S4, and Mamba.

evaluations.setting: MQMTAR length generalization (pp. 8-9, Section 4.3; pp. 17-18, Appendix B.3): four layers, width 512, eight heads, vocabulary 263, 50M examples, one epoch, batch 256, learning rate 1e-3, weight decay 0.1, train through length 64; mean of three seeds with maxima also shown.
evaluations.metric: Sequence exact-match accuracy at 1x, 2x, 4x, 8x, 16x, 32x, and 64x training length.

evaluations.setting: Reverse and sorting extrapolation (p. 9, Table 2; p. 17, Appendix B.3): reverse uses four layers, vocabulary 36, 30M examples and tests 1x/1.5x; sorting uses two layers, vocabulary 36, 40M examples and tests 1x/2x/4x; otherwise width 512, eight heads, one epoch, batch 256, learning rate 1e-3; mean of three seeds.
evaluations.result: At reverse 1.5x, the best compact kernel is triweight 3-ReLUmax at 0.29, below Transformer 0.52. At sorting 2x/4x, biweight 2-ReLUmax is 0.93/0.34, 1-ReLUmax 0.80/0.30, sparsemax 0.92/0.29, and triweight 3-ReLUmax 0.95/0.30.
evaluations.baseline: Transformer is 0/0 at sorting 2x/4x; Gaussian is 0.06/0; Gaussian kNN is 0.80/0.01; uniform kNN is 0/0.

evaluations.setting: MQMTAR positional-bias ablation (p. 18, Appendix C.1/Table 8), evaluated from 1x through 64x.
evaluations.metric: Mean exact-match accuracy across three seeds.
evaluations.baseline: Transformer with ALiBi: 1.00,1.00,0.99,0.09,0.01,0,0; architecture differs from the two Memory Mosaic rows.

evaluations.setting: OOD language-model transfer from BabiStories to 512-token Simple English Wikipedia sequences (p. 19, Appendix C.2/Figure 5).
evaluations.metric: EMA-smoothed per-token average cross-entropy by token position.
evaluations.result: Compact kernels are described as comparable to Gaussian, with ReLUmax qualitatively best overall; no exact values, dataset sample count, seeds, or uncertainty are supplied.
evaluations.baseline: Gaussian, Gaussian kNN k=32, uniform kNN k=32, normalized ReLU, sparsemax, biweight, and triweight Memory Mosaics.

evaluations.setting: Efficiency discussion (p. 18, Appendix B.4) for contexts of 512 tokens in language modeling and up to a few thousand tokens in synthetic tasks.
evaluations.metric: No measured runtime, peak memory, FLOPs, throughput, or realized attention density.
evaluations.result: The authors state attention is not dominant and fused-kernel wall-clock gains are modest in this regime; long-context speedups are only projected through compatibility with AdaSplash.
evaluations.baseline: Conceptual comparison with AdaSplash/FlashAttention and sorting-heavy top-k selection; no in-paper systems benchmark.

limitations: [Author-stated, p. 10, Section 6] Every evaluated model is below one billion parameters; scaling compact kernels beyond the available compute budget remains untested.
[Author-stated, p. 5, Equation 6; p. 15, Appendix B.1] Fixed normalized ReLU can have empty support; the experimental uniform fallback avoids NaNs but is a different, dense behavior.
[Author-stated, p. 18, Appendix B.4] Contexts are short enough that attention is not the dominant cost and expected fused-kernel wall-clock gains are modest.
[Reviewer-identified] The unit-norm premise and tied query/key contextual memory make the exact kernel correspondence narrower than ordinary Transformer attention with separately learned projections.
[Reviewer-identified] The work measures neither realized support cardinality nor speed/memory, so its sparsity and efficiency narratives are not empirically linked.
[Reviewer-identified] BabiStories uses validation curves without numeric endpoints, seeds, dispersion, or tests; the eight-layer 2-ReLUmax learning-rate exception further complicates fairness.

[Reviewer-identified] RegBench hyperparameters are optimized for Gaussian then reused, which can under-tune new kernels; improvements over Gaussian and Transformer are generally small and lack uncertainty.
[Reviewer-identified] Synthetic length results use only three seeds, show large mean-to-best-seed gaps, and reverse extrapolation directly favors the Transformer.
[Reviewer-identified] The ALiBi ablation changes architecture as well as sparsity mechanism, so it cannot attribute gains solely to compact support.
[Reviewer-identified] The appendix OOD result is a smoothed plot with no exact values or experimental sample/seed details.
[Reviewer-identified] The neurobiological discussion is analogy rather than a tested model of hippocampal indexing or pattern separation.
failure_modes: Fixed normalized ReLU returns 0/0 when every score is below its threshold; the chosen uniform fallback abruptly makes the head dense and can retrieve irrelevant values.
Fixed-cardinality uniform kNN discards score magnitude and fails even in distribution on MQMTAR (0.04 at 1x for k=32), showing that sparsity alone is insufficient.
Discrete top-k Gaussian selection has nonsmooth membership changes and exhibits mild training instability at intermediate depth.
ReLUmax can require optimizer retuning: the eight-layer order-2 variant was unstable at the shared learning rate.
Compact support can eliminate information needed by algorithms such as reversal; all tested compact variants trail the Transformer at 1.5x reverse length.
Positional locality can conflict with content-addressed retrieval: ALiBi reduces Epanechnikov MQMTAR accuracy at every extrapolated length.
Method rankings are seed-sensitive on long sorting sequences; a favorable best seed can exceed the mean by more than 0.6.
Without efficient sparse kernels and sufficiently long contexts, mathematical zeros do not produce meaningful wall-clock savings.
reusable_insights: Separating kernel shape, bandwidth normalization, and support anchoring yields a useful design space: each controls locality, support size, and degeneracy differently.
Unit-sphere normalization makes radial-kernel theory directly usable for dot-product attention and reveals when an apparent activation is exactly a classical estimator.
Adaptive normalization is more consequential than sparsity by itself: entmax consistently beats fixed normalized ReLU and uniform kNN in these experiments.
Anchoring a threshold to the maximum score is a general way to guarantee nonempty variable-cardinality selection without sorting for a fixed k.
Length-generalization claims should be decomposed by algorithmic task; associative recall, reversal, and sorting demand different support patterns.
Sparse-model papers should report realized density alongside end-task quality and should measure fused-kernel throughput at lengths where attention dominates.
Mean-plus-best-seed tables can expose optimization instability, but per-seed values or dispersion are needed to distinguish robust mechanisms from lucky runs.
open_questions: Do the same compact-kernel transformations improve a standard Transformer with independent query/key projections, rather than only tied-query/key Memory Mosaics?
How do support size and sparsity evolve by layer, head, training step, and context length for entmax and ReLUmax?
At what context length and sparsity does AdaSplash make each compact kernel faster and more memory-efficient than FlashAttention-2 under matched hardware and quality?
Can the normalized-ReLU empty-support case be handled continuously without the dense uniform fallback?
Does learning r/alpha, the ReLUmax bias b, or bandwidth per head outperform the fixed classical kernel orders without destabilizing training?
Why do compact kernels help MQMTAR yet trail dense Transformer attention on reverse extrapolation, and can a mixed dense/sparse head allocation cover both?
Do the small RegBench gains survive kernel-specific hyperparameter tuning, multiple seeds, and significance tests?
Do compact kernels retain their modeling behavior at 8B-10B scale and one-trillion-token training, where Memory Mosaics have separately been scaled?

competitive_landscape.title: Test-time regression: a unifying framework for designing sequence models with associative memory
competitive_landscape.difference: It supplies the broad test-time-regression design framework spanning softmax, linear attention, state-space models, and online learners. This paper's narrower addition is the exact bounded-support-kernel account of sparsemax/entmax/ReLUmax plus compact-kernel experiments.

competitive_landscape.title: Long-Context Generalization with Sparse Attention
competitive_landscape.difference: It directly tests alpha-entmax and learnable-temperature ASEntmax in Transformers, including up to 1000x synthetic and 8x language-model length extrapolation. It overlaps the adaptive-sparsity claim and provides stronger long-context evidence; the present paper contributes the classical compact-kernel derivation and ReLUmax within Memory Mosaics.

competitive_landscape.title: Dense Associative Memory with Epanechnikov Energy
competitive_landscape.difference: It already connects an Epanechnikov-inspired log-sum-ReLU energy to exact sparse associative retrieval and exponential memory capacity. The present paper generalizes the regression correspondence across multiple polynomial kernels and attention maps, but does not provide that storage-capacity analysis.

competitive_landscape.title: AdaSplash: Adaptive Sparse Flash Attention
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct systems complement and efficiency benchmark
competitive_landscape.difference: AdaSplash implements alpha-entmax with custom Triton kernels and measures runtime/memory against optimized softmax. The present paper uses AdaSplash and invokes its results, but contributes no new fused kernel or efficiency measurement of its own.

competitive_landscape.title: Sparse Sequence-to-Sequence Models
competitive_landscape.difference: It defines the alpha-entmax family, algorithms, gradients, and sparse sequence-to-sequence applications. The current paper reinterprets discrete alpha values as classical compact kernels and studies them in associative memories rather than introducing entmax itself.

competitive_landscape.title: From Softmax to Sparsemax: A Sparse Model of Attention and Multi-Label Classification
competitive_landscape.difference: It introduces sparsemax as Euclidean projection and derives its Jacobian/loss. The present paper's incremental contribution is the auto-normalized Epanechnikov-regression interpretation and comparison to other support mechanisms.

competitive_landscape.title: Memory Mosaics
competitive_landscape.difference: It introduces the contextual/persistent associative-memory architecture used by every compact-kernel experiment here. The present work changes its contextual retrieval kernel; it is not an independent validation in a conventional Transformer.

competitive_landscape.title: Memory Mosaics at scale
competitive_landscape.difference: It scales Memory Mosaics v2 to 10B parameters and one trillion tokens, showing that the architecture itself can scale. It does not test the compact kernels here, so it narrows any inference that this sub-1B kernel study already establishes large-scale behavior.

competitive_landscape.title: Scalable-Softmax Is Superior for Attention
competitive_landscape.difference: It addresses attention dispersion by scaling softmax with input length while retaining dense support and reports language-model/retrieval long-context gains. It challenges the implication that exact zeros are necessary; the present paper instead changes kernel support and offers a kernel-estimation interpretation.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims the first formal link between sparse attention and compact-support kernel regression, a unification of normalized ReLU, sparsemax, alpha-entmax, top-k attention, and a new max-anchored r-ReLUmax family, with generally superior empirical performance.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Proposition 1 and Appendix A give a clean exact derivation for unit-normalized inputs, and Section 3.2 distinguishes adaptive bandwidth from fixed-k and maximum-anchored support. Experiments cover three problem families, but are all sub-1B Memory Mosaics, show mixed task outcomes, and contain no measured systems advantage.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The defensible novelty is the compact-kernel taxonomy and exact alpha-entmax/rectified-polynomial correspondence, plus the ReLUmax parameterization. Sparsemax, alpha-entmax, Memory Mosaics, Epanechnikov associative memories, long-context sparse attention, and efficient entmax kernels all predate it. Current direct work provides stronger Transformer long-context and systems evidence, so claims should be restricted to the mathematical unification and small-scale Memory-Mosaic evidence, not general superiority or practical speedup.
